review_mode: Independent agent reading of the complete four-page exercise, exact commitment/dispatch verification and primary-source comparison
result: Scientific assumptions, exact optimum, infeasible approximation, startup formulation and total-time arithmetic pass

calculation.execution_level: Classical exact rational arithmetic, all binary commitments and analytical continuous economic dispatch; no MILP package, QAOA simulator or QPU was run
checks: All sixteen commitment patterns were enumerated. Continuous dispatch was solved from its exact feasible interval and the marginal-cost slope, without discretizing output.
Only B is on in period one; both generators are on in period two. Dispatch (A,B)=(0,30) then (80,10) MW gives USD 3000 variable cost and USD 220 startup cost, totaling USD 3220.

For every commitment pattern, all sixteen startup-indicator patterns were checked. With the stated strictly positive startup costs, the unique startup-cost minimizer under v>=u-u_previous is the actual off-to-on transition pattern.
Restoring startup charges to the approximate plan gives USD 2770, but A produces 30 MW below its 40 MW minimum in period one. The USD 450 difference is not a feasible saving.
The sequential hypothetical stages sum to 44 seconds, fourteen seconds above the target and slower than the hypothetical fifteen-second classical baseline.

As an additional illustrative example, assigning a fixed USD 10000 cost to infeasible commitments gives an exactly quartic multilinear evaluated-cost function on the four original bits. A per-commitment classical evaluation is therefore not automatically an exact QUBO on those bits.

scientific_findings.finding: The stated exact balance excludes dumping, storage, unserved load and external trades. Minimum output therefore rules out starting A in the low-demand first period. Restoring a cost term without restoring all constraints does not repair the approximate plan.

The exercise is a two-period mixed-integer linear model with binary commitment/startup variables and continuous MW dispatch. Its candidate sampling and exact dispatch validation are an educational adaptation; they do not reproduce the cited paper's complete variational algorithm.

Four bits count only the commitment register. Output discretization, auxiliary variables, phase-cost construction, circuit depth, routing, measurements and classical evaluations need their own accounting. The five-second QPU stage includes compilation, measurement and mitigation only by the exercise's explicit assumption.

Compare feasible plans under the original objective and equal inputs, accuracy and constraints. Timeout/failure rates and certified optimization gaps must accompany cost and latency; all operational thresholds and timings here are educational assumptions.

This differs from assuming that a fully minimized continuous-dispatch value function is automatically quadratic.

en.title: The cost of a feasible generation plan
en.summary: Commitment choices and continuous power output meet through operating constraints. Restore minimum-output limits and startup costs to test an approximate plan, then compare the QAOA–classical split using original-model costs and end-to-end time.

listing.review: Both titles and summaries are faithful to the problem and contain no numerical answers or adoption verdicts.

checks: Both languages preserve numerical answers, exact units, assumptions and the initially closed solution structure.
The formal explanation explicitly identifies binary commitment/startup variables, continuous MW output, initially off generators and the previous-period status.
Positive startup prices ensure transition equivalence at an optimum; the text does not claim that the lower-bound inequality forces equality in every feasible assignment.
The paper's joint continuous/slack/variational optimization is distinguished from the exercise's per-commitment exact linear dispatch validation.
The QAOA cost-operator construction and nonquadratic value-function issue are retained; four commitment bits are not presented as the whole resource cost.

All eleven paper authors and original title words are retained. Expanded formal algorithm-name capitalization is preserved consistently with the PDF as a named method; the remaining title uses sentence case.
References appear in order 1 then 2 and both language bibliographies match.
A relevant existing power-operation discussion is linked through matching language routes; its underlying hardware papers were not newly reviewed.
The exact primary-source access route and the absence of hardware/benchmark reproduction are disclosed.
